Hi Jordan — great to meet today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

1) Goals you shared: 85th %-ile realtime SLO = 250ms for short user prompts (~32 tokens avg) and batch scoring for longer analytics jobs (avg 2k tokens) with budget guardrails.
2) Clarify volumes: you estimated 20M interactive tokens/month and 120M batch tokens/month (peak batch windows up to 2 hours).
3) Budget band you mentioned on the call: target $/1M tokens in the range of $300–$600 (you indicated $400 preferred if latency SLOs are met).

Attached I’m including a rough unit-econ breakdown and an initial SLO mapping matrix (velocity_poc_slos.xlsx, poc_unit_econ_breakdown.pdf). These are conservative estimates we use for qualification — we’ll run more exact numbers once we have token distribution histograms.

Immediate asks / next steps:
- Jordan: confirm the monthly token split (interactive vs batch) and whether the interactive SLO needs to be global or US-only.
- Procurement: if you want baseline pricing/PO terms, loop in your procurement contact and we’ll surface standard enterprise T&Cs.
- My team: Marissa (SE) will propose two concrete serving options (low-latency tier + streaming; cost-optimized tier + batching) with per-1M token math and expected p50/p95/p99 latency.

Can we target Tues 4/20 for a 30-min follow-up to review the numbers? If that works, I’ll send a calendar invite.

Thanks — looking forward to moving this forward.

Jordan — thanks, adding the explicit comparison below (high level). See attached PDFs for the spreadsheet with the math (poc_unit_econ_breakdown.pdf).

Option A — Low-latency (Streaming + Dedicated Pool):
- Config: Dedicated GPU pool, streaming responses, small batching window (10–20ms), KV caching for repeated prefixes.
- Expected latency: p50 ~ 60–90ms, p95 ~ 180–260ms for 32-token interactive prompts (depends on model selection/sequence length).
- Unit economics (approx): $/1M tokens = $520 (baseline for quantized medium model on NVL100 equivalent).
- Pros: meets your 250ms 85th %-ile SLO; predictable tail latency; easier to tune for realtime UX.
- Cons: higher per-token cost; higher reserved capacity requirements.

Option B — Cost-optimized (Batching + Shared Pool):
- Config: Shared capacity, larger batching windows for interactive fallbacks (50–200ms tail), batch scoring for analytics (2k-token jobs).
- Expected latency: interactive p50 ~ 120–180ms, p95 ~ 300–450ms (depends on load and batching). Batch jobs: throughput optimized.
- Unit economics (approx): $/1M tokens = $310 (with aggressive batching and prefix caching).
- Pros: lower cost per token, good for high-volume batch workloads.
- Cons: higher and less predictable p95 tail for interactive; may not meet your 250ms 85th %-ile without dedicated lanes.

Hybrid suggestion (recommended for POC):
- Dedicated small interactive tier (sized for 20M tokens/month) to hit 85th %-ile SLO; routing policy to fallback to cost-optimized tier for non-critical traffic.
- Expected blended $/1M tokens ~ $380–$420 depending on traffic mix and autoscale burst.

Notes / assumptions:
- Numbers assume a medium-size open model with 8k context and standard KV cache hit rates (30% effective prefix reuse).
- We used conservative GPU pricing and added 12% infra overhead and estimated S3 egress for cached payloads.
- Final per-1M pricing can be adjusted after we get token histograms and model selection.

Attachments: poc_unit_econ_breakdown.pdf (detailed line-item calc), velocity_poc_slos.xlsx (SLO mapping).

Happy to walk through the spreadsheet in Tue’s call. If you want, I can also prepare a 2-slide summary for your procurement to expedite internal sign-off.

—
